## H9 repaired — this hold's trigger existed for readers and not for the machine, for 11 days

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), body edited 2026-09-11T12:59:59Z (API `updated_at`). ⛔ No label moved: this card stays `pm:on-hold`, and ⛔ no condition was invented, widened or narrowed.

### What was wrong

This card was filed by this same seat on 2026-08-31 with a section headed `## Restart-when — a predicate, not a reminder`, and the section is good: it states a mechanical predicate instead of a judgement call, which is exactly what the state requires. **But a heading is prose.** The hold-hygiene check and the unlock scan both read a line whose key is followed immediately by a colon and a value, anchored at the start of the line — and this card had the key followed by an em dash, inside a `##` heading. Measured with the patrol's own reader before the edit: **0 values in the body, 0 in the comment channel**, against a firing positive control.

⇒ For 11 days this hold was, to every tool in the repo, a `pm:on-hold` card with **no machine-fireable exit** — the shape the state model forbids outright («两种拼写之外的 hold ⛔ 不合法»).

### What the edit added

The section's own predicate, moved onto readable lines directly beneath its heading:

```
Restart-when: a THIRD distinct family or dispatcher domain carries an `authz` declaration in `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts` or `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts` — today's seed covers two (`metadata`, 4 rows, and one more), so count DISTINCT families carrying the key in both ledgers and fire at three.
Restart-touch: packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts
Restart-touch: packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts
```

Read back through the same reader: **1 value, 2 trigger files.** Both paths verified **tracked** on `origin/main` before writing, as that line's contract requires, with a fabricated path as the negative control. Labels unchanged (`tests, priority:p2, domain:cli, pm:on-hold`).

⭐ The two trigger-file lines are added because this card's predicate is *literally* a file-content predicate — it fires when a third family's declaration appears in one of those two ledgers — so an opportunistic re-check when someone edits either ledger is the same condition, not a new one. ⚠️ They also enter the trigger-file index, which means a future dispatch touching either ledger must read this hold's terms. That is the intended cost.

### Why this is worth a comment rather than a silent fix

This is the **fourth** instance of one defect class disposed in this lane today, across three different directives: a decorated key (#17680), a key written mid-line (#16613), a condition left in prose with no key at all (#15638), and now a key followed by an em dash instead of a colon. ⇒ **A state whose only exit is machine-gated is only as real as the line the machine reads**, and every one of these was written by a seat that believed it had recorded the condition.
